result.target_summary: CCG revenue decreased $2.5 billion from 2022, with Notebook revenue of $17.0 billion (down $1.8 billion, volume -5% due to lower demand partially offset by normalization in H2 2023, ASPs -5% due to education mix) and Desktop revenue of $10.2 billion (down $495 million, volume -9%, ASPs +5% due to commercial/gaming mix); Other CCG revenue decreased $229 million due to smartphone modem ramp down and lower connectivity demand.

target_year_over_year_context.explanation:
The 2023 disclosures D010 (Notebook), D011 (Desktop), and D012 (Other CCG/Modem) individually report CCG segment revenue changes for 2023 vs 2022. The 2024 disclosure D036 explicitly reports the total CCG revenue change for 2023 vs 2022 and breaks it down into the same specific components: Notebook, Desktop, and Other CCG, citing identical drivers (education mix, commercial/gaming mix, modem ramp down).

Both disclosures cover the Client Computing Group (CCG) segment financial results for the prior year comparison (2022 vs 2021 for D043, 2023 vs 2022 for D036). They detail revenue changes driven by notebook and desktop volumes and ASPs, with similar drivers like inventory normalization and demand fluctuations. D043 covers 2022 performance, D036 covers 2023 performance, both being the specific CCG revenue trend disclosures for their respective prior-year comparisons.

comparisons.peer_topic: Embedded segment net revenue and drivers for fiscal year 2024
comparisons.peer_summary: Embedded net revenue decreased by 33% to $3.6 billion in 2024 from $5.3 billion in 2023, primarily due to lower demand as customers normalized inventory levels.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel (CCG) and AMD (Embedded) attribute revenue declines to a cycle of lower demand followed by customer inventory normalization. Intel’s CCG Notebook and Desktop volumes decreased 5% and 9% respectively, driven by lower demand but partially offset by increased volume in H2 2023 as inventory normalized. Similarly, AMD’s Embedded segment revenue decreased 33%, explicitly citing lower demand as customers continued to normalize inventory levels.

sentences.text: ▪CCG revenue decreased $2.5 billion from 2022. Notebook revenue was $17.0 billion, down $1.8 billion from 2022. Notebook volume decreased 5% from 2022, driven by lower demand across market segments, partially offset by increased volume in the second half of 2023 as customer inventory levels normalized compared to higher levels in the first half of 2023. Notebook ASPs decreased 5% from 2022 due to relative strength in the education market segment resulting in a higher mix of small core products combined with a higher mix of older generation products. Desktop revenue was $10.2 billion, down $495 million from 2022. Desktop volume decreased 9% from 2022, driven by lower demand across market segments, partially offset by increased volume in the second half of 2023 as customer inventory levels normalized compared to higher levels in the first half of 2023. Desktop ASPs increased 5% from 2022, due to an increased mix of product sales to the commercial and gaming market segments. Other CCG revenue was $2.1 billion, down $229 million from 2022, primarily driven by the continued ramp down of our legacy smartphone modem business and lower demand for our wireless and connectivity products as a result of lower notebook volumes.
Embedded net revenue of $3.6 billion in 2024 decreased by 33%, compared to net revenue of $5.3 billion in 2023.
The decrease in net revenue was primarily due to lower demand as customers continued to normalize their inventory levels.

comparisons.peer_summary: Gaming net revenue decreased by 58% to $2.6 billion in 2024 from $6.2 billion in 2023, primarily driven by lower semi-custom product revenue.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel and AMD report significant revenue declines in segments heavily tied to computing hardware (Notebooks/Desktops for Intel, Gaming for AMD), driven by volume/shipments and ASP pressures. Intel’s CCG Notebook revenue dropped $1.8 billion (volume -5%, ASP -5%), while AMD’s Gaming revenue dropped 58% ($6.2B to $2.6B) due to lower semi-custom product revenue. Both companies experienced contractions in these core consumer-adjacent segments.

comparisons.peer_topic: QCT segment revenue drivers and EBT margin change
comparisons.peer_summary: QCT revenues in fiscal 2024 increased primarily due to higher handset revenues driven by $2.8 billion in higher chipset shipments from major OEMs and higher automotive revenues from new vehicle launches with Snapdragon products, partially offset by lower IoT revenues; QCT EBT as a percentage of revenues increased primarily due to these higher revenues.
comparisons.comparison: Both Intel (CCG) and Qualcomm (QCT Handsets) highlight customer inventory normalization as a key driver affecting revenue and shipments. However, Intel’s CCG volume still declined year-over-year, whereas Qualcomm’s QCT revenue increased.
